title: Recording with Wardell Gray and Charlie Parker for Ross Russell's Dial
summary: He picked up Wardell Gray for near daily dates, did 15 or 20 sides, and recalls the session with Parker, Garner and Earl Coleman.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Anyway, I'm going to move on to Wardell Gray. Wardell didn't drive, you know, so I used to pick Wardell up, and I guess we recorded just about every other day for Ross Russell and Dial Records. I can remember on the way to one record date I was humming something. I think it was maybe part of a theme that Paramount used to use in their news feature. [SINGS REFRAIN] Anyway, we got to the date, and sure enough, Wardell remembered it and interpolated it in some piece that we played. I don't remember the name, but in any Dial record theme you will certainly remember this. That's one of the interesting things that happens in this business.
You said you were recording every other day for Ross Russell's Dial label. For how long? How many records do you think that produced?
Oh, I guess we must have done 15 or 20 sides. I don't remember how many records, because during that period we must have done four-five-six-seven-eight
(they were 78's then) sides with Charlie Parker, Erroll Garner, what's the singer Earl Coleman...Earl Coleman...
He did 'This is Always' on the back side of one of Charlie Parker's records. Do you remember that?

Doc West, of course. I guess it's not funny, but all these guys are gone [NOT EARL COLEMAN IN 1982], and it seems like I'm still around just getting started. Well, I guess I always feel that way about music, you know, because if I should live to be 200 I'll never learn all there is to know. That's what makes it so interesting.
